findings.title: Dynamic imports are started eagerly, so nothing is actually lazily loaded
findings.body: `appStore` is now an object literal whose values are the *results* of calling `import("./app")` at module-evaluation time. Calling `import()` immediately starts loading the module, so every single app package (applecalendar, googlecalendar, stripepayment, …) is still pulled in as soon as `@calcom/app-store` is imported — the only thing that changed is that consumers now have to `await` the already in-flight promise. The PR's goal of async/lazy app loading is not achieved, while the extra `async`/`await` plumbing added across CalendarManager, videoClient, handleCancelBooking, bookings.tsx etc. buys nothing. To actually defer loading, the map must hold thunks (e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`) and call sites must invoke them, e.g. `await appStore[key]()`.

findings.title: Rejected app-import promises are created with no handler attached (unhandled rejection at startup)
findings.body: Each value in `appStore` is a promise created at module load and stored for an indefinite amount of time before any consumer awaits it. If any one app module fails to evaluate (missing/incorrect peer dependency, module-scope code that throws, bad env configuration), the corresponding promise rejects with no `.catch()` attached, producing an unhandled promise rejection at process start — which terminates the Node process on Node >= 15. Previously a broken app module failed loudly and synchronously at import time with a clear stack trace; now it can either kill the server or silently surface later as a generic "Could not get connected calendars" error from `getConnectedCalendars`'s catch block. Promises for apps that are never used are never awaited at all, so their rejections are always unhandled.

findings.title: Example comment points at a non-existent path
findings.body: The template comment was changed from `// import * as example from "./_example";` to `// example: import("./example"),`. The example app lives in the `_example` directory, so anyone uncommenting/copying this line will get a module-not-found error. The commented path should be `./_example`.

findings.title: getCalendarCredentials now returns a Promise in the `calendar` field, changing its public contract
findings.body: `getCalendarCredentials` is exported and returns `{ integration, credential, calendar }`. Because `getCalendar` became async, `calendar` is now `Promise<Calendar | null>` instead of `Calendar | null`. Only `getConnectedCalendars` in this file was updated to `await item.calendar`; any other caller that reads `.calendar` keeps a promise, which is always truthy, so guards like `if (!calendar)` silently pass and subsequent `calendar.listCalendars()` style calls fail at runtime. Additionally, these promises are created eagerly for every credential inside a non-async function, so if a caller only needs `integration`/`credential`, a rejected `getCalendar` promise is never handled. Either make the function async and await the calendars, or keep the field lazy (a thunk) and update all consumers.

findings.title: Recurring-cancellation branch still uses forEach(async) so calendar deletions are never awaited
findings.body: In the recurring/allRemainingBookings branch the code iterates credentials with `.forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); … apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent) })`. `forEach` does not await the async callbacks, so the handler continues immediately and `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` at the end of the handler runs while `apiDeletes` is still empty for this path. Consequently, for recurring bookings the external calendar events are deleted fire-and-forget (and in a serverless runtime may never be deleted at all, since the response is returned before the awaited dynamic app import resolves), and any `deleteEvent` failure becomes an unhandled promise rejection instead of being surfaced. The adjacent legacy branch in this same PR was correctly converted to `for (const credential of calendarCredentials)`; the same conversion is needed here.

findings.title: requestReschedule deletes calendar/video events in an unawaited forEach(async) callback
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...) })` is not awaited, so the mutation proceeds to send the reschedule-request email, fire webhooks and return before the deletions are even initiated. Previously `getCalendar` was synchronous, so the `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` requests were at least started before the handler continued; now the first thing the callback does is await a dynamic module import, meaning in a serverless/edge runtime the function can be frozen or torn down after the response and the stale calendar entries / video meetings will never be removed. Rejections are also unobserved (unhandled promise rejection). Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (ref) => …))` or a `for … of` loop.

findings.title: forEach(async) makes the surrounding try/catch dead and leaves deletions unawaited
findings.body: The loop was changed to `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); … })`. The enclosing `try { … } catch (error) { logger.error(...) }` can never observe errors thrown inside an async callback, so the explicit error logging is dead code and failures surface as unhandled promise rejections. The function also continues to send the reschedule email and return `true` before the awaited dynamic app import resolves, so the calendar/video cancellations are fire-and-forget and may not run to completion in a short-lived (serverless) process. Replace with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (ref) => …))` so the try/catch works and the work is actually awaited.

findings.title: forEach(async) makes the surrounding try/catch dead and leaves deletions unawaited
findings.body: Same problem as in the vital app: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); … })` is wrapped in a `try/catch` that can no longer catch anything, because errors raised inside the async callbacks reject the (discarded) returned promises instead of propagating synchronously — they become unhandled promise rejections. Additionally the booking is marked cancelled and the reschedule email is sent before the awaited dynamic app import resolves, so the external calendar/video cancellation requests may never be issued. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (ref) => …))`.
